To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pressure pain threshold (PPT) map is useful for the design of insoles, and the pressure discomfort threshold (PDT) map can be used to assess the sensitivity of the foot.

1) PPT, PDT, and stiffness were measured at 95 points of the plantar surface, 2) PPT, related PDT and tissue stiffness showed strong correlation, 3) five distinct clusters of points were identified based on the three dependent variables and 4) the foot template showed high similarity for all participants.
the PPT and related pressure pain discomfort thresholds map are useful to determine the most appropriate location of the insole in order to prevent pressure discomfort and pain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for measuring PPT, PDT, and tissue stiffness on a standard grid-type template on the plantar foot surface.
the development of a methodology to assess the pressure pain thresholds and tissue stiffness on foot.
the development and validation of a methodology to assess pressure discomfort thresholds, pressure pain thresholds and tissue stiffness on 95 points of the plantar surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PPT and related PDI map are useful to identify the regions of the foot which are more susceptible to pain.
the plantar foot can be divided into five distinct regions based on the three parameters evaluated.
the PPT and related Pressure discomfort threshold map are useful to identify regions of the foot where the footbed should be designed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to develop a methodology to assess PPT, PDT, and tissue stiffness on a plantar grid.
the PPT and PPT maps can be used to design the foot bed of shoes.
this study provides a reliable and valid template for the assessment of PPT, PDT, and stiffness on the foot.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the foot template is a reliable method to assess the pressure discomfort thresholds (PDT) of the foot.
the foot template is reliable and can be used to assess PPT and PDT on the foot surface.
the foot can be divided in five clusters of locations that can be used as a guide to design insole and shoe components.
